title: TICK stage 2: run run_reconciliation_tick on its own thread at a 60 s cadence, serialized with entry dispatch by a journal_sync lock (removes ~28 s from the trader tick)
note: [from TICK-DURATION-115S, docs/research/tick-duration-115s-profile-2026-11-04.md section 6] MEASURED 2026-11-04 tick_cost (37 ticks): order_monitor reconciliation half 28.4 s per tick on the main loop. A plain move off-thread is UNSAFE: the reverse reconciler's default ORPHAN_POSITION_POLICY=adopt acts on first sight, and package->trade row takes up to 7.6 s (audit F8, n=40), so a concurrent pass could adopt a duplicate of a fill the main thread has not journaled. Design: one journal_sync lock held by Coordinator.multi_account_execute (place+journal) and by each reconciliation pass (preserves today's invariant); entries wait <= one pass only when a pass is in flight. Needs a replay/equivalence test over recorded ticks. Sweep cadence must stay bounded (60 s), never stopped (Prime Directive). DETECTOR: tick_cost order_monitor ~0 on-loop and tick mean < 40 s over >= 20 ticks. [input from TICK-DURATION-115S stage-1 observation 2026-11-05] After the faster loop (cycle 159 s -> 59 s) one sqlite "database is locked" burst appeared 02:20:41-02:21:04Z: _sweep_package_close_reason_from_trade, _sweep_unlinked_packages, _sweep_stuck_linked_packages failed once each, then venue_protection_snapshot.record_read (timeout=5.0). All contained, retried next pass. Baseline: 0 in a complete journalctl scan 2026-11-04 21:44-23:22Z (21,226 lines). Cause unestablished. Before adding a third DB-writing thread, measure lock frequency over a longer window and identify the lock holder; the journal_sync lock design should also bound sqlite contention. [lane session_01AFoLuLzq1snbogF2qX97Pi 2026-11-05] MEASURED (diag relay issues #23192/#23193): tick_cost one process from 06:51:30Z, 78 ticks: mean 47414.7 ms, order_monitor 23631.5 ms mean. exit_loop_health: 158 intervals, 1 breach, max 71164.1 ms at 08:01:12Z = max_pass_ms 41989.8 at the same instant. The breach is the EXIT PASS itself, not the main tick: journalctl 08:00:30-08:01:12Z shows each of ~15 packages taking 2-7 s (normal whole pass ~1 s) while the main thread logged 'database is locked' at 08:01:05/08:01:11. So stage 2 alone does NOT fix the exit interval. LOCK FREQUENCY, journalctl 'database is locked', 2026-11-04T00:00Z to 2026-11-05T08:12Z (windows 14:30Z-02:00Z and 02:00Z-now complete, 162,226 + 173,173 lines; 00:00-14:36Z window returncode -15, a lower bound): 59 lines in ~16 bursts (10 s to 2 min each); 55 are signal_audit_logger dual-write failures (a waiter), 4 are the 02:20Z order_monitor burst. Lock HOLDER NOT IDENTIFIED: the read-only relay cannot see sqlite lock owners; ml_decision_shadow and db_integrity are ruled out (no journal write / mode=ro). Fix in PR: reconciliation on its own 60 s thread under a journal_sync RLock held by Coordinator.multi_account_execute and run_pairs_tick, AND exit-thread best-effort telemetry writes (position_telemetry, position_path_history, venue_protection_snapshot) get a 0.25 s busy timeout instead of 5 s. Dry soak scripts/ops/soak_reconcile_offtick.py (40 s foreign hold every 90 s, ~1000 s simulated): pre-change exit writes max interval 70.2 s, 7/30 over 60 s; with the change 34.1 s, 0/33.
